title: capabilities — the observable vocabulary, and which configurations produce which of it (4.5.3, 4.6.7)
description: Read by S3.0 to screen configurations and by the bridge to test answerability. The vocabulary sits at the top level and the configurations point into it by name: a definition written once cannot drift between two configurations that claim the same observable. On the microscope side every configuration is one entry in the optical-path table, and check 38 holds the two id sets equal. The vocabulary itself lives in contracts/observables.json, not here: one name with one estimator, in one place. A configuration points at it with produces, and check 38 rejects an id the registry does not define.

status.description: skeleton: no configuration is declared and S3.0 refuses rather than guessing. provisional: the configurations are declared but the vocabulary is a first slice (plan.md 11-1), so an observable's absence is not an impossibility and the bridge must hold rather than refuse. populated: the vocabulary is fixed and absence means the other side cannot produce it.

role.description: imaging produces observables. perturbation drives the system and produces none of its own -- optical trapping is blocked from every detector -- so it overlays an imaging configuration instead of replacing one (4.5.3).

optical_path.description: the id of this configuration in the optical-path table. Null on the simulation side, which has no such table.

devices.description: control channels a plan in this configuration may have to drive, at the granularity of one worker per channel (4.6.8). A4 screens these on automatable and read_back.

oneOf.description: an id this configuration produces on its own

requires_composition.description: perturbation configurations that must be composed in for this to be producible. Check 38 requires each to be a perturbation whose composes_with names this configuration.

produces.description: ids from contracts/observables.json, plain when the configuration produces them alone and objects when a perturbation has to be composed in. The composition requirement lives on the observable rather than in a new path id: envelope/optical_paths.json's composable block already says which configurations compose, and a second id saying it again is two tables that will drift (4.6.7).

composes_with.description: for a perturbation configuration: the imaging configurations it can overlay. The combination has to be a valid tuple in the optical-path table as well.

axes_applicable.description: optional and normally omitted. The axis list is fixed and an axis that does not apply abstains (4.5.3); pruning axes here would drop a constraint where nothing records that it was dropped.

requires_contrast.description: What the sample has to provide for this configuration to see anything. S3.0 reads it as the discriminator for the goal's `contrast` priority, which is the one priority term it can evaluate before S3 runs (4.5.3). The fact was already in `label` as a sentence, where deterministic code could not reach it, and the fan-out cap went unresolved for want of it. An imaging configuration that omits it is not screened on contrast and the cap stays unresolved; a perturbation configuration produces nothing and needs none.
